what: cbor::decode<parking_lot> of carsales (the fields and xorshift data of Cap'n Proto), 20000 messages read in turn. Arm A: main 25a2d78. Arm B: A with a DepthMax template parameter on cbor::decode<T> (default 64), carried through value_read; a reference that is followed at DepthMax gives error::nesting_depth_exceeded. Time in ns per car.
why: The security review found that cbor::decode<T> of a struct that holds a list of itself recursed as deep as the bytes said, and 100000 levels overflowed a stack of 8 MiB. The owner asked for the fix to be measured.
how: Google Benchmark, one binary per arm, each built twice (a, b), 3 rounds alternating, --benchmark_min_time=0.1s --benchmark_repetitions=3, random interleaving, GLIBC_TUNABLES trim_threshold, mmap_threshold and top_pad high. The whole run was made twice.
finding: Run 1 medians: A 117.13 / 117.35, B 118.9 / 119.96, B against A +1.9 percent, noise 0.2 and 0.9 percent. Run 2 medians: A 117.6 / 117.93, B 117.0 / 119.52, B against A +0.4 percent, noise 0.3 and 2.1 percent. The difference is not above the noise in both runs.
